blurTest.evidence: At gallery scale each asset has one unmistakable headline, one dominant product state, and one concise proof point.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The neo-brutal outlined frames, lavender-green gradients, oversized circular picker, and winner art form a recognizably NameSnap silhouette.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: The ordered story reads immediately as celebrate, paste names, quick pick, spin, prevent repeats, and reset safely.

realityTest.evidence: All screen content comes from simulator-rendered app states with a fictional 16-person roster; numbering, history, eligibility counts, and reset behavior agree.

journeyTest.evidence: The six screenshots and 20.4-second preview cover setup through winner reveal and repeat-round management without exposing a purchase surface.

platformTest.evidence: The release set uses exact Apple-accepted iPhone 6.9-inch and iPad 13-inch dimensions, no alpha, and device-specific layouts captured from the native app.

buyerValueTest.evidence: A prospective user can see the emotional payoff first and then verify fast entry, two draw modes, numbered fairness, history, and reset control.

implementationTest.evidence: The Swift app build, capture scripts, image generator parse, screenshot dimensions, alpha checks, and H.264/AAC preview probes all passed.

screenFindings: The celebration-first direction was selected after comparing a utility-first direction, a classroom-first direction, and a celebration-first direction against current Spin The Wheel, Duolingo, and Partiful references.
The suite carries the real app's tokens and original celebration art into its marketing frame without importing another product's recognizable composition or visual vocabulary.
The iPhone and iPad hero assets show the winner modal, confetti, and guitarist celebration as the emotional payoff while keeping the actual app UI visible.
The dedicated history fixture keeps recent winners and the active pool visible without a scroll artifact or Dynamic Island overlap.
No screenshot, poster frame, or preview segment shows the paywall, prices, or an upgrade prompt.
The preview masters run 20.4 seconds and use only recorded native app views plus a documented bundled CC0 audio track.
repairs: Rejected the first reset-confirmation capture because an unrelated settled-wheel winner appeared behind the modal; moved the fixture to the stable quick-pick surface.
Rejected the first history capture because automated scrolling placed content beneath the Dynamic Island; added a deterministic history-preview fixture that hides setup panels.
Rejected the first preview timing pass because static simulator timestamps shortened the export below Apple's minimum; added cloned-frame padding to produce stable 20.4-second masters.
Re-encoded both previews to H.264 High Level 4.0 at a measured 10.89 Mbps with 30 fps video and 48 kHz stereo AAC audio.
Removed stale upgrade captures from the active release pipeline and made the image generator clear prior release PNGs before rebuilding.
verdict: Approved after gallery-scale, original-scale, and time-sampled video review. The release pack is celebration-led, product-authentic, technically App Store-ready, and contains no paywall imagery.
